items.title: Noetherianness ascends and descends along a representable surjective flat finite type morphism
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: For a morphism of affine formal algebraic spaces which is representable, surjective, flat and locally of finite type, the lemma asserts that the source is Noetherian if and only if the target is (statement lines 4654-4659). The proof first observes that a Noetherian affine formal algebraic space is adic*, so that by the corresponding statement for the adic* property one may assume both spaces are adic* (proof lines 4661-4665). It then invokes the criterion for Noetherianness of such a space, writes the target as a countable colimit as in the corresponding presentation lemma, base changes the morphism to each stage -- which is an affine scheme because the morphism is representable and affine -- and notes that the stages present the source as a colimit and that each induced morphism of stages is faithfully flat and of finite type (proof lines 4667-4677). The conclusion follows from the two algebra statements giving that Noetherianness ascends and descends along such a ring map (proof lines 4677-4679). The claim is H2: the argument reduces one type to another, then applies a criterion to convert the geometric statement into a statement about the stages, where the two directions are the two cited algebra statements.
